fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Behind Every Lead Form
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the capture and the hand-off to sales as one app, from a description of how leads reach you today.
fields.feature_1:
One lead table for every source

Chat, the website form, the quote form, and webinar signups all write to the same lead table. Every row carries the same fields, so a lead reads the same whatever its source.
fields.feature_2:
The source and campaign on each lead

The app saves where each lead came from, down to the page and the UTM campaign in the link. Reports then count leads by that source without anyone tagging a row by hand.
fields.feature_3:
A duplicate check before a lead is created

Before it writes a new lead, the app looks up the email address. A match adds the new signup to the existing record, and its history keeps every way that person came in.
fields.feature_4:
Leads written to your CRM through its API

The app writes each lead to HubSpot or any CRM with an API and reads back the owner and stage. Sales keeps working where it already works, with the source fields filled in.
fields.feature_5:
A message when a lead needs a person

Pick the leads that should reach someone right away, such as demo requests. The app sends that person a Slack message or an email with the answers and a link to the record.
fields.feature_6:
The lead app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of your lead generation app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Anyone on your team can read how leads are matched and stored, and change it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Ways Leads Arrive and Get Counted
fields.tab_content_1:
Four chat answers reach HubSpot as one lead

Corlander Scheduling puts a chat on its pricing page that asks 4 questions, one per screen. Imogen Faulkes, clinic director at Bramcote Physio, answers each one: 6 clinics, paper schedules today, a start this quarter, and yes to a demo. The app writes her lead to HubSpot with all 4 answers and the page she chatted on.
fields.tab_content_2:
Outside its 14 zip codes, a quote request gets an email

Sorrelton Roofing covers 14 zip codes, and its quote form asks for the zip code first. Ottavine Halvorsrud asks about a roof leak from 60540, not one of the 14. The app saves her request as out of area and emails her the towns it covers. Only requests from inside the area, like 60187, reach the estimator, Fergus Cobbins.
fields.tab_content_3:
Rhea signs up twice and stays one lead

Rhea Vandermolen became a Mirefield Analytics lead 3 weeks ago, when she downloaded its pricing guide. She registers for Thursday's webinar with the same email. The app finds her record and adds the webinar to it instead of creating a second lead. Her record now lists 2 sources: the guide and the webinar.
fields.tab_content_4:
Paid search falls to 58 of 212 weekly leads

Every Monday at 9 am, Wendling Fleet Parts gets a Slack digest in #marketing that counts last week's 212 leads by source. The website form brought 71, paid search 58, webinars 46, and dealer referrals 37. Paid search is flagged: 58 against 90 the week before.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Lead Generation Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps from the places leads reach you today to lead generation automation that saves each lead once, built with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every place a lead comes in
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the fields every lead carries
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide what counts as a duplicate
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the app in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every place a lead reaches you today: the contact form, the quote form, chat, webinar signups, event lists, and referrals. Next to each, note where the lead goes now and who sees it first. Start with the source that brings the most leads.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the fields every lead holds whatever its source: name, email, company, source, and the campaign in the link. Keep the forms short. A question the form does not need can wait for the chat or the first sales call.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose the field that makes two signups the same person. Email address is the plainest match. Then decide what a match does: attach the new signup to the record already there, keep both sources on it, and leave the lead's owner as it is.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the sources and the duplicate rule in a prompt, along with any check that runs first, such as a service area. Emergent builds the forms and the chat with the logic behind them, and you change any part by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect HubSpot or whichever CRM your sales team works in through its API, so each lead lands there with its source fields filled. Then add Slack or email for the leads that need a person right away, such as a demo request.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run last month's leads through it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last month's leads through the app before it goes live. Count how many duplicates it finds, check that every lead carries a source, and open a few records in the CRM to confirm the fields landed where sales expects them.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the first weekly digest with whoever runs each channel. If a source drops from one week to the next, check its form and its links first. Leads that arrive with no campaign point to a link missing its tag. Adjust the app by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What is marketing automation for lead generation?
faq_plan.ref: What is marketing automation for lead generation?

prov.original: What is marketing automation for lead generation?

faq_plan.a: It is software that captures each new lead and moves it forward without anyone copying details by hand. Lead generation automation saves the person's details and where they came from, checks for an existing record, and passes the lead to a CRM or straight to a salesperson.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up lead generation automation?
faq_plan.a: List every place leads come in, pick the fields each lead must carry, and decide how to spot a repeat signup. Describe that setup in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, connect your CRM, and send a week of old leads through it as a test.

faq_plan.q: Which lead sources should lead generation automation handle first?
faq_plan.a: Start with the one where leads sit longest before anyone sees them, such as a contact form that someone copies into the CRM each morning. The busiest source comes next. Emergent builds every source into one app with no task cap, and adding another is one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: Should lead generation automation score leads as they come in?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once the duplicate check has run. A repeat signup then adds to the score the person already has instead of starting a new one. Keep the point rules as their own step, and lead scoring automation can change without anyone touching the forms.

faq_plan.q: What should the chat ask in lead generation automation?
faq_plan.a: Ask only questions whose answers change what happens next: company size, the tool used today, the timeline, and whether the visitor wants a call. Save each answer as it comes in. Sales then sees where a visitor stopped. Emergent builds the chat as a conversational flow, one question per screen.

faq_plan.q: How many fields should a form ask for in lead generation automation?
faq_plan.a: Ask for as few as the next step needs. A demo request needs a name, a work email, and a company, while a quote request also needs the street address. Ask anything else later, on the first call or in a follow-up form.

faq_plan.q: What happens to a lead after lead generation automation captures it?
faq_plan.a: It should reach an owner while the person still remembers filling in the form. Save it, run the duplicate check, then assign it with lead routing automation by territory or round robin, and message the owner with the lead's answers.

faq_plan.q: How does lead generation automation keep duplicate leads out of a CRM?
faq_plan.a: It checks for a match before the lead is written, not after. Lowercase the email address and trim spaces first, since Rhea@ and rhea@ reach the same person but fail a strict match. For the backlog, export your contacts once, merge them on email, and import the clean list.

faq_plan.q: How does lead generation automation track where each lead came from?
faq_plan.a: It saves the source at the moment of capture: the page the lead came through and the UTM parameters in its link. Tag every link you control, ads and emails included, with one naming scheme. The app keeps those fields in a database you own, ready to count by week.

faq_plan.q: What should lead generation automation do with leads not ready to buy?
faq_plan.a: It should keep them, mark them as not ready, and add them to a lead nurturing workflow that sends something useful until they reply or act. Record the reason they gave, such as timing or budget. A later email can then speak to it.

plan.angle: The live SERP for lead generation automation is software roundups, agency explainers and video tutorials that list tools in general terms. This page shows the capture end of the funnel as a working app: a pricing-page chat that writes a lead, a quote form that checks the service area first, a duplicate check that adds a second signup to the existing record, and a Monday digest that counts leads by source. It stays on getting leads in clean and attributed, and leaves scoring, routing and nurture emails to the lead scoring automation, lead routing automation and lead nurturing workflow pages. The FAQ covers lead gen vs demand gen, chat qualification, capture fields, duplicates and source tracking as operator advice.
